about: Every model experiment so far (work/47): task, model, open weight or not, events checked, cost total and per 100 events, result. Counts only: no prompts, page text or model output. Costs are from the model ledger (OpenRouter's reported cost). A model's word is evidence, never fact.

experiments.task: Second opinion: does the event's public page agree with our entry (status, start, end, place)?
experiments.approach: the model judges match / mismatch itself
experiments.result: 125 events flagged, almost all noise (time formats such as 6:30 PM vs 18:30, place wording). Status: 163 match, 3 mismatch, 4 unparsed.

experiments.task: Same task, new design: the model only extracts what the page says; the comparison is done in code on times normalised to UTC minutes
experiments.result: 14 flagged, of which 3 worth a person's look (yorkseed salon, ai-engineers lunch, elevon night). Most others were model slips (wrong year, room names read as places).

experiments.task: Same check, the hourly run with researcher.2's re-reads
experiments.result: 17 flagged; the 3 earlier ones still among them.

experiments.task: First calls through the router (cheap tier) and the credit guard
experiments.approach: a hello call, then the credit check
experiments.result: The OpenRouter account was out of credit (402); the router recorded it and then refused calls below its minimum credit. A mock call (no network) also passed.

comparison.title: 8B against 70B on the same 170 events
comparison.lesson: The extra cost is about 9 times and still under a tenth of a cent per event. Most of the gain came from the design (extract, then compare in code), not only from the bigger model.
